messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want a fair financial share. I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount, and I won’t subsidize that from my share. I’m not in a rush, but I want this settled fairly. B being able to use money matters too; I’m not against her getting access to her share, but I can’t decide for her or agree to terms on her behalf. I care about my relationship with A and don’t want this to hurt us, but that doesn’t mean I’ll sign off on something unfair.

I want a stable home with my husband and more financial independence. A family discount could make buying it realistic; I’d also like the house to stay in the family. C’s agreement matters, and she hasn’t agreed. I’m not sure what else is at stake yet.

Thank you. I’d like some money from the house, if that’s possible, to help me start a dance studio. I’m not sure what amount would be possible. I don’t want to put pressure on either of my sisters, and I’d like us to stay on good terms.

1. The wording is too general. Use this: “C wants a fair financial share, won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase, and has not agreed to it.”  
2–5 fit. For 2, I want B’s wish to use money considered, but I won’t decide for her. For 3, I want B’s own choices respected. For 4, I want time and a fair process. For 5, I don’t want this to damage my relationship with A. My discomfort is with being expected to accept a discounted buyout; I’m not in a rush.
The wording for 6–9 fits. I’m not sure whether anything else is at stake, and I don’t have a specific discomfort to add right now.

Those wordings fit, thank you. A studio would give me a chance to build the work I care about; clear information would help me plan, and I don’t want my sisters to feel pressured or our relationships harmed. I still don’t know what amount, if any, might be possible. Nothing else comes to mind, and I’m comfortable with this wording.

#1 fits. Use this: “C wants her financial share treated fairly and her consent to be genuinely hers.” I don’t want to be pressured into accepting a discounted buyout because that could make me subsidize A. #4 fits that too; I want time to consider things without pressure. I haven’t held anything else back. My discomfort is with pressure to agree, not with the pace.

Nothing else comes to mind, and I’m okay with the pace. The family discount matters because it may make buying the house feasible for us; I don’t want C pressured to agree. I don’t have another discomfort to add right now.

I haven’t held anything else back, and I’m comfortable with the pace and wording. Not knowing what amount, if any, might be possible makes it hard to plan realistically for the studio; I’d appreciate clear information when it’s available.
No new concerns from me. #14 repeats #4; otherwise my entries fit. I can’t speak for A or B.
I don’t want C to feel pressured because her choice and our relationship matter to me. #9 covers that; it fits. Nothing else comes to mind, and I’m okay with the pace.

Yes, #11 covers #16 too. The information would help me plan realistically for the studio. Please use: “B wants clear, trustworthy information about what may be possible, when it becomes available.” I haven’t held anything else back and remain comfortable with the pace and wording.

I’m not choosing an option yet. O1 works as a pause. I’m uncomfortable with O2 implying an independent valuation settles what’s fair or means I agree to a purchase. It doesn’t; I need to be free to reject that path. No other concerns, and I’m not in a rush.

I have a small concern with O2: “at an independently established value” sounds like it rules out a family discount before we discuss one. I’d like it considered as a request, with C entirely free to say no. I’m otherwise okay with the pace and have nothing else to add.

I’m comfortable with these as draft options and don’t have a preference yet. I haven’t held anything else back; I’d just appreciate being told directly when there’s clearer information about whether funds might be possible.
